title: 4D-STEM Insights into Amorphous Structure and Recrystallization Dynamics
content: Amorphous materials are critical to a wide range of applications, including advanced battery technologies, high-performance coatings, and functional materials [1,2]. These materials often undergo amorphization under extreme conditions, which significantly alters their physical and chemical properties. Semiconductors and ceramics, such as GaAs and Bi2O3, are especially susceptible to amorphization, leading to shifts in their bulk functionality. Despite the lack of long-range atomic order, amorphous materials often exhibit short- and medium-range ordering (S/MRO) that plays a key role in determining their macroscopic properties [3]. As a result, understanding the nature of these short- and medium-range structures is crucial for the design of novel materials with tailored properties.
